sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: Talk-See is a mobile art space that has been formed inside a passenger car (Samand) as a small gallery.
In this space, small paintings - drawn on one-thousand Toman banknotes -  are displayed either framed or as postcards on a handmade stand, replacing the front passenger seat.
The project's audience consists of passengers (using ride-hailing taxi apps like Snapp/Tapsi), who enter this situation entirely by chance.
During the journey, a conversation develops between the driver/artist and the passengers.
There is an opportunity to purchase the artworks if desired.

Simultaneously, during stops (for example, during rush hours or while waiting at a red light), the artist paints on banknotes using a clipboard mounted on the steering wheel, and this process becomes part of the live experience of the project.

sections.title: Context & Site
paragraphs: Set within the urban space in motion, the project takes place inside a personal car temporarily transformed into a gallery circulating through the city streets.
This space creates a kind of intermediary state between public and private: an enclosed environment, yet situated in the heart of everyday life.
This setting was chosen because it provides access to an audience that does not usually visit art galleries.
Instead of inviting the audience to an art space, the project places itself directly in the path of their daily commute.
There were times when the car was parked alongside an art event, such as an exhibition by the artist in his hometown, Bojnourd, allowing the project to be redefined in various situations.

sections.title: Motivations & Questions
paragraphs: At its core, the project grows out of a desire to step beyond the limited circle of gallery audiences.
This project seeks to test the possibility of presenting and even selling artwork among people who do not normally engage with such spaces.
Furthermore, the project utilizes the familiar social experience of chatting in a taxi and turns it into a platform to raise issues regarding art, the economy, and everyday life.
Several questions arise here: Is it possible to transform an everyday situation into a space for an artistic experience?
What possibilities for exchanging views are created by a short conversation while on the move?
And how can art enter the normal flow of life without relying on official institutions?

sections.title: Constraints & Strategies
paragraphs: The project was realised without any institutional financial support and is entirely funded by personal resources, which, despite the limitations, has created a sense of practical independence.
So far, no specific obstacles in the form of censorship have been reported, though economic conditions alongside social and urban structures have influenced its development.

The primary strategy is to utilize existing, low-cost situations in everyday life: dead time during transit, the ready-made space of the taxi, and the initial trust that exists between a driver and a passenger.
The mobile nature of the project also allows it to relocate and adapt to different conditions, making it flexible in the face of potential limitations.

sections.title: Fundings & Partners
paragraphs: The project is self-organized and funded by the artist.

sections.title: About the Artist
paragraphs: Bio:
Ali Moammery (born 1981, Bojnourd) is a graphics graduate, painter, and art instructor with over two decades of artistic experience.
He lives in Mashhad and Bojnourd, engaging in teaching and artistic activities.

His works have been showcased in solo and group exhibitions across various cities and numerous galleries, including Sis Art Space and Golshan Gallery in Bojnourd, Naron and Artin galleries in Mashhad, O, Aria, and Haft-Samar galleries in Tehran, as well as Sepideh Ahadi Gallery in Berlin.
His urban project, Talk-See, has been ongoing since 2017.
Email: Moammery1362@gmail.com
Website/Instagram:
https://www.instagram.com/Ali_moammery
https://www.instagram.com/talk.see.projects/
Encounters mainly involve the general public and taxi passengers—people from various walks of life who enter the space by chance.
Their participation takes shape through encountering the artworks in an unexpected space, observing them, and, most importantly, conversing with the artist.
The interior space of the car, acting as a semi-private environment, facilitates short but focused conversations.
This project resembles a "happening" situation where each encounter is a unique event.
The audience can transition between different roles, ranging from a spectator to an active participant, and even to an art buyer.
The live painting process during the ride also helps to build trust and lay the groundwork for further interaction.
In some cases, the conversations are audio-recorded (with the audience's consent), accompanied by video recorded by a dash-cam mounted on the car.
The camera is pointed toward the sky ahead, ensuring no faces are shown.
Participation in this project is momentary and discontinuous; each encounter is an independent experience that cannot be easily repeated for the same individual.
